question: How are the weights of a feed-forward neural network found, and how is overfitting controlled?

limits: Chapter is conceptual: no experiments, no benchmark numbers; figures are ConvNetJS toy visualisations.
Derivations cover only sigmoidal neurons with squared error and no bias; softmax/cross-entropy, ReLU and tanh derivatives left as exercise or deferred.
Learning-rate and optimiser treatment deferred to Chapter 4 of the book (adaptive rates, momentum); no Adam, no LR schedules, no initialisation, no batch norm.

Dated: early stopping via validation set is described only informally; 'L2 empirically performs better than L1' is unsupported here; dropout probability p is keep-probability (differs from PyTorch's drop-probability convention); the 'grid search' hyperparameter search is superseded by random search in common practice (not stated in chapter).
practices: Never train and evaluate on the same data; split into training, validation and test sets (p.31-33).
Divide training into epochs and stop when validation accuracy stops improving while training accuracy rises (p.31).
Choose hyperparameters by grid search on the validation set and report the test accuracy once (p.32).
Prefer L2 over L1 unless feature selection/interpretability is needed (p.35).
Use inverted dropout: divide surviving activations by p at train time so no test-time scaling is needed (p.36-37).
If training error stops improving rethink architecture/features; if validation error stops improving regularise; if test error is poor get more data (p.33-34).
Treat bias as a weight on an input fixed at one (p.22).
